# Round

Rounds a number to a given number of digits after the point.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Round(value, decimals, [mode])
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | The number to round. Null, or a value that is not a number, is a runtime error. |
| `decimals` | number | How many digits after the point to keep: an integer from -2147483648 to 2147483647. Zero rounds to a whole number; a negative count rounds to tens, hundreds and so on, so -2 rounds to a multiple of 100. A number with a fractional part, a number outside that range, null, or a value that is not a number is a runtime error. |
| `mode` | string, optional | How a value exactly halfway between the two nearest candidates is rounded; every other value goes to the nearer one. Exactly one of these strings, case included: `"halfUp"`, away from zero; `"halfEven"`, to the candidate whose last kept digit is even; `"halfDown"`, toward zero. When it is left out, or null, it is `"halfUp"`. Any other string, or any value of another type, is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Number. The value rounded to decimals digits after the point. When value already has no more digits than that, it is returned unchanged. The result is exact when value is exact and the result can be held exactly; otherwise it is the nearest floating-point value. A result too large to hold is a runtime error. Never null.

## Remarks

An exact number is rounded by its exact value. A number that is not exact is rounded by the value it actually holds, which can lie slightly above or below the number as written, so a value that looks halfway may round the other way.

## Example

`Round(1.25, 1)` returns `1.3`.

`Round(2.5, 0, "halfEven")` returns `2`.

`Round(1250, -2)` returns `1300`.
